title: Lucci Jackson and young players like Vic Dispenza
summary: He doesn't recall Lucci or Albert Jackson, and mentions a young reader, Vic Dispenza's son.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Ask him if he knows Lucci.
He knows Lucci? Who? Lucci. Lucci? Trombone. Lucci? Yeah. Lucci.
Albert Jackson, they call him. Albert. Maybe if I learn by some other name, I might know him, you see.
He worked in a young tuxedo with John.

See, he worked in a young tuxedo with John Cashman. Oh, yeah, lately, huh? Oh, I don't know him. You know, I got a whole lot of these school boys coming out now. I got a little fella, Victor Spender's son. He's good, yeah, but Vic never really get caught up there. He had his name, eh? He ain't never really get caught up there. He's a child. He's a good reader, but he couldn't play.
Vic Dispenza. I don't know him.
What's his son's name? His son can grow, San Bernard. What's his son's name? He named after his daddy, Vic Dispenza. He must be around about 24, 25 years old now, that boy.
